The Rigveda is the earliest and most important Vedic text, consisting of hymns composed over a long period by multiple seers. These hymns are primarily addressed to Vedic deities and reflect the religious, social, and philosophical ideas of early Vedic society, making it a layered compilation rather than a single-time composition.

Key Points:

• The Rigveda is the oldest of the four Vedas.

• It consists of 1028 hymns (suktas).

• Hymns are composed in Vedic Sanskrit.

• The text evolved over several centuries, not at one time.

• Hymns are attributed to different rishis and priestly families.

• Major deities include Indra, Agni, Soma, Varuna, and Surya.

• The Rigveda reflects early Indo-Aryan religious practices.

• It provides insights into early social and political structures.

• The text was transmitted through oral tradition.

• It forms the foundation of later Vedic literature.

The Permanent Settlement (1793), introduced by Lord Cornwallis, sought to secure a fixed and predictable land revenue by recognizing zamindars as landowners. This policy aimed to align zamindars' interests with British rule and stabilize colonial finances.

Key Points:

• The Permanent Settlement was introduced in 1793.

• It applied mainly to Bengal, Bihar, and parts of Odisha.

• Zamindars were recognized as hereditary landowners.

• Land revenue was fixed permanently.

• Zamindars were responsible for collecting revenue from peasants.

• The policy aimed to create a loyal landed elite.

• It ensured regular revenue flow to the colonial state.

• Failure to pay revenue led to auction of zamindari rights.

• Peasants received no ownership security.

• The system reshaped agrarian relations under British rule.

Under international anti-doping regulations, athletes bear strict personal responsibility for compliance. They must provide accurate whereabouts information and personally participate in sample collection. Delegation of sample collection to any official is not permitted under anti-doping codes.

Key Points:

• Anti-doping rules are governed by the World Anti-Doping Code.

• Athletes have personal responsibility for compliance.

• Accurate whereabouts information is mandatory.

• Athletes must be available for out-of-competition testing.

• Sample collection requires direct athlete participation.

• Delegation of sample collection is not allowed.

• These rules prevent tampering or manipulation.

• Strict liability applies regardless of intent.

• Procedures ensure fair play and integrity in sport.

• Anti-doping compliance is central to international competition eligibility.

Why Nations Fail is a seminal work in political economy, co-authored by Daron Acemoglu and James Robinson. The book argues that inclusive political and economic institutions, rather than geography or culture, are the primary determinants of long-term national prosperity.

Key Points:

• Why Nations Fail (2012) analyses why some countries achieve sustained prosperity while others remain poor.

• The authors emphasize the role of inclusive vs extractive institutions.

• Inclusive institutions encourage innovation, property rights, and broad participation.

• Extractive institutions concentrate power and wealth in the hands of elites.

• The book uses historical case studies from Europe, Africa, and the Americas.

• It challenges explanations based solely on geography, culture, or climate.

• James Robinson is also co-author of The Narrow Corridor, which examines the balance between state power and liberty.

• Daron Acemoglu has written extensively on institutions, democracy, and inequality.

• Fareed Zakaria, mentioned in the options, authored The Post-American World, focusing on global power shifts.

• Abhijit Banerjee co-authored Poor Economics, which analyzes poverty through microeconomic evidence.

• Raghuram Rajan authored Fault Lines, addressing global financial imbalances.

• Each of these works contributes to development economics and global political economy, but only James Robinson is the co-author of Why Nations Fail.

• It has influenced debates on governance reforms and institutional capacity.

In the Parliament of India, the guillotine is a procedural device used during the budgetary process to ensure timely disposal of demands for grants. When the allotted time for discussion expires, remaining demands are put to vote together without further debate, maintaining legislative efficiency.

Key Points:

• Guillotine applies specifically during the discussion on demands for grants.

• It operates after the expiry of the prescribed discussion time.

• Undiscussed demands are deemed voted without detailed scrutiny.

• The practice ensures time-bound passage of the budget.

• It reflects the executive's control over financial business.

• Guillotine is distinct from cut motions, which seek reductions.

• It prevents legislative deadlock on financial approvals.

• The device is rooted in Westminster parliamentary practice.

• It prioritizes fiscal continuity over prolonged debate.

• The procedure underscores the importance of budget timelines.

Annie Ernaux received the Nobel Prize in Literature, 2022 for her distinctive literary voice that combines personal memory, social observation, and historical insight, written with remarkable clarity and restraint.

Key Points:

• Annie Ernaux is a prominent French writer.

• She was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2022.

• Her writing explores memory, identity, and social class.

• The Nobel citation highlighted "clinical acuity" in her work.

• She often blends autobiography with collective history.

• Her prose style is direct, precise, and unsentimental.

• Themes include gender, education, and social mobility.

• Her works challenge boundaries between personal and political.

• Ernaux's literature reflects post-war French society.

• The award recognized her ethical courage and narrative innovation.

Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi, the premier of Assam, strongly opposed the Cabinet Mission Plan's proposal to group Assam with Bengal, which could have pushed Assam towards East Pakistan. His resistance ensured Assam's separate political identity within India.

Key Points:

• The Cabinet Mission Plan (1946) proposed grouping provinces.

• Assam was to be grouped with Bengal under the plan.

• Bengal had a Muslim League majority.

• Bordoloi opposed this grouping to protect Assam's interests.

• He mobilized public opinion and political pressure.

• Assam demanded separate constitutional status.

• The opposition prevented Assam's inclusion in Group C.

• This ensured Assam remained within Indian territory.

• Bordoloi is known as the architect of modern Assam.

• His stance shaped India's northeastern political boundaries.

After the 1991 economic reforms, rationalization and reduction of fertilizer subsidies increased input costs for farmers. This directly affected the agriculture sector, particularly small and marginal farmers dependent on chemical fertilizers.

Key Points:

• The 1991 reforms aimed at fiscal discipline.

• Fertilizer subsidies were reduced and rationalized.

• Input costs for farmers increased significantly.

• Small and marginal farmers were most affected.

• Crop production costs rose in many regions.

• Profit margins in agriculture were squeezed.

• Subsidy reduction impacted foodgrain cultivation.

• The move aimed to reduce budgetary burden.

• Agriculture faced adjustment pressures post-reforms.

• The sector required compensatory policy support afterward.

The Wangala Festival is a prominent harvest festival of the Garo tribe of Meghalaya. It is celebrated to mark the end of the agricultural year and to honor Saljong, the sun god, for a successful harvest. The festival reflects the agrarian culture, ritual traditions, and collective social life of the Garo community.

Key Points:

• Wangala Festival is celebrated by the Garo tribe of Meghalaya.

• It is also known as the Hundred Drums Festival due to the use of traditional drums.

• The festival marks the completion of the harvest season.

• It is dedicated to Saljong, the sun god of the Garo people.

• Celebrations include rhythmic drum dances, rituals, and community feasts.

• The festival symbolizes gratitude to nature and ancestral spirits.

• Wangala reinforces tribal identity and cultural continuity among the Garos.

• The Bhotia tribes of Uttarakhand are primarily associated with transhumance, wool trade, and Himalayan pastoral culture, not Wangala.

• Bhotias celebrate festivals such as Losar and Phool Dei, linked to Tibetan-Buddhist traditions.

• The Bait (or Beda/Beda-like nomadic groups) of Jammu and Kashmir are traditionally associated with crafts and itinerant lifestyles, not harvest rituals like Wangala.

• The Nyishi tribe of Arunachal Pradesh celebrates festivals such as Nyokum Yullo, linked to agriculture and nature worship.

• Nyokum Yullo is dedicated to harmony between humans and nature, distinct from the Wangala tradition.

• Each tribe's festivals reflect region-specific ecology, belief systems, and livelihood patterns.

• Wangala remains uniquely tied to the agrarian worldview of the Garo tribe.

The Khelo India Winter Games 2024 witnessed strong institutional participation, with the Indian Army emerging as the top performer. While Jammu & Kashmir has been a dominant force in previous editions, its medal position and gold count in 2024 did not align with the statement given, making only the first statement correct.

Key Points:

• Khelo India Winter Games are part of the Khelo India initiative to promote winter sports.

• The 2024 edition featured competitions in snow-based sporting disciplines.

• The Indian Army topped the medal tally with 10 gold medals.

• Army teams benefit from structured training and high-altitude exposure.

• Jammu & Kashmir has historically performed well in winter sports events.

• The region has hosted earlier editions due to natural snow conditions.

• In 2024, J&K did not secure the second position with nine golds as stated.

• Institutional teams play a major role in medal tallies.

• The Games aim to develop winter sports talent in India.

• They support preparation for international winter sporting events.

Puducherry is renowned for its well-preserved French colonial architecture, a legacy of its period under French rule. The city's urban layout, buildings, and streets reflect strong European planning and aesthetic influences.

Key Points:

• Puducherry was a former French colonial settlement in India.

• The city features French-style villas and administrative buildings.

• Grid-pattern streets characterize the French Quarter.

• Buildings commonly use pastel colours and arched verandas.

• The architecture reflects European town-planning principles.

• French influence remains visible in urban culture and heritage.

• The area is often referred to as the French Quarter (White Town).

• Architectural preservation supports heritage tourism.

• The city contrasts with surrounding Tamil architectural styles.

• Puducherry represents a unique Indo-European cultural synthesis.

The David Dixon Award is presented at the Commonwealth Games to honor the outstanding athlete of the Games, recognizing excellence in performance, leadership, and sportsmanship.

Key Points:

• The David Dixon Award is named after David Dixon, a former CGF official.

• It is awarded during the Commonwealth Games.

• The award recognizes the best overall athlete of the Games.

• Selection considers sporting excellence and conduct.

• It is given to individual athletes, not teams.

• The award highlights values of fair play.

• It enhances the prestige of individual achievement.

• Recipients often represent exceptional all-round performance.

• The award is distinct from medal tallies.

• It symbolizes the spirit of the Commonwealth movement.

A higher position in the World Press Freedom Index reflects a country's stronger protection of media independence, journalistic safety, and freedom of expression. The index evaluates how freely journalists can work without undue political, legal, or economic pressure.

Key Points:

• The World Press Freedom Index is published annually.

• It assesses the state of press freedom across countries.

• Higher ranking signifies less restriction on media operations.

• It reflects independence of journalism from state control.

• Safety of journalists is a key evaluation parameter.

• Legal protections for media freedom influence rankings.

• Editorial independence is a major indicator.

• Plurality of media voices improves ranking outcomes.

• Lower censorship contributes to better rankings.

• The index highlights global trends in media freedom and democracy.

The Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram, built during the Pallava period, represents a crucial transition in South Indian (Dravidian) architecture. It demonstrates the evolution from rock-cut cave temples to fully structural stone temples, marking a milestone in Dravidian architectural development.

Key Points:

• The Shore Temple is located at Mahabalipuram, Tamil Nadu.

• It was constructed under the Pallava dynasty.

• The temple is an example of Dravidian architecture.

• It is built using carved granite blocks.

• Earlier Pallava monuments were mainly rock-cut caves.

• The Shore Temple represents structural temple architecture.

• It shows continuity from monolithic rathas to stone temples.

• The complex includes shrines dedicated to Shiva and Vishnu.

• It reflects experimentation in temple construction techniques.

• Mahabalipuram is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Tana Bhagat led a socio-religious reform movement among the Oraon tribe in the Chotanagpur region, which lies in present-day Jharkhand. The movement emphasized non-violence, moral reform, and resistance to British authority and exploitative landlords.

Key Points:

• Tana Bhagat Movement emerged in the early 20th century.

• It was led by Tana Bhagat, an Oraon tribal leader.

• The movement arose in the Chotanagpur plateau.

• This region falls in present-day Jharkhand.

• It opposed forced labour and landlord exploitation.

• The movement promoted non-violence and self-discipline.

• Participants rejected certain traditional rituals.

• It showed influence of Gandhian principles.

• The movement represented tribal assertion and reform.

• It contributed to anti-colonial consciousness among tribals.

Standardized rules of Kho-Kho, as governed by national sports authorities, specify the total duration of the match including intervals as 48 minutes. Other statements related to pole specifications and sub-junior block distance do not align uniformly with official rulebooks.

Key Points:

• Kho-Kho is a traditional Indian tag sport.

• Official rules are framed by the Kho-Kho Federation of India.

• A standard senior match duration including intervals is 48 minutes.

• Match time is divided into innings and breaks.

• Pole specifications vary slightly across categories and revisions.

• Sub-junior block distance differs from junior categories.

• Rules aim to ensure player safety and fairness.

• Uniform regulations support competitive standardization.

• Kho-Kho emphasizes speed, agility, and coordination.

• The sport is played widely in schools and national tournaments.

Modern currency systems operate on fiat money, where currency value is based on government authority and public trust, not on direct convertibility into commodities like gold or silver.

Key Points:

• Modern currencies follow a fiat money system.

• Fiat money has no intrinsic commodity value.

• It is not backed by gold or silver reserves.

• Currency value depends on legal tender status.

• Central banks regulate money supply and credit.

• Gold standard systems are no longer in operation.

• Fiat currency allows flexible monetary policy.

• Exchange rates are influenced by market forces.

• Public confidence is key to currency stability.

• Modern systems support global trade and finance.

Odissi, one of the classical dance forms of India, is fundamentally structured around two characteristic postures: Chowk, representing strength and symmetry, and Tribhanga, symbolizing grace and lyrical movement. These postures define the aesthetic grammar of Odissi.

Key Points:

• Odissi originated in the state of Odisha.

• Chowk is a square stance symbolizing masculine energy.

• Tribhanga involves three body bends at neck, torso, and knee.

• Tribhanga expresses feminine grace and fluidity.

• Both postures are rooted in temple sculpture traditions.

• Odissi dance draws inspiration from Jagannath temple art.

• The dance emphasizes sculptural poses and rhythmic precision.

• Facial expressions convey bhava and rasa.

• Odissi is traditionally accompanied by Odissi music.

• Chowk and Tribhanga form the core movement vocabulary.

In Maratha society, Kunbis were primarily agricultural and pastoral communities who formed the backbone of the rural economy. They were closely linked to land cultivation and cattle rearing and played a significant role in the social and military mobilization of the Maratha polity.

Key Points:

• Kunbis were a major peasant community in the Deccan region.

• They were associated with agriculture and pastoral activities.

• Kunbis formed the rural base of Maratha society.

• Many Maratha soldiers originated from Kunbi backgrounds.

• The community contributed to agrarian production and revenue.

• Kunbis were socially distinct from temple priestly classes.

• They were not a merchant-banking community, unlike banias.

• They differed from Rajput warrior clans in origin and function.

• Kunbis supported the rise of Maratha power.

• Their role reflects the agrarian character of Maratha polity.

• Rajput clans were primarily martial elites, not peasant groups.

• Temple priests belonged to Brahmanical communities.

• Merchant bankers were linked to trade and finance, not cultivation.

Life-size sculptures of Yakshas and Yakshinis, often depicted holding a chauri, are characteristic of the Mauryan Period. These figures reflect early Indian sculptural traditions emphasizing volume, polish, and symbolic guardianship.

Key Points:

• The Mauryan Period dates to 4th - 2nd century BCE.

• Yakshas and Yakshinis were nature and fertility deities.

• Sculptures are typically life-size or larger-than-life.

• Use of Mauryan polish gives a smooth, glossy finish.

• Yakshini figures often hold a chauri (flywhisk).

• The sculptures emphasize robust physical forms.

• They served as guardian figures at religious sites.

• Stone carving showed advanced technical skill.

• These works mark the beginning of monumental sculpture in India.

• They influenced later Buddhist and Jain iconography.

The Green Revolution was initiated during the Third Five-Year Plan (1961 - 1966) to achieve foodgrain self-sufficiency. It focused on technological interventions in agriculture, especially for wheat and rice, to overcome chronic food shortages.

Key Points:

• The Third Five-Year Plan spanned 1961 - 1966.

• It aimed at self-reliant economic growth.

• The Green Revolution emphasized HYV seeds.

• Expansion of irrigation facilities was critical.

• Use of fertilizers and pesticides increased sharply.

• Initial success was seen in wheat production.

• Punjab, Haryana, and western UP benefited early.

• The First Plan (1951 - 56) focused on agriculture but not HYVs.

• The Second Plan (1956 - 61) emphasized heavy industries.

• The Fourth Plan (1969 - 74) focused on consolidation and stability.

The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) and made it obligatory for states to establish them as institutions of rural local self-government. It laid down a uniform structure, powers, functions, and electoral framework to strengthen grassroots democracy across India.

Key Points:

• The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 came into force on 24 April 1993.

• It inserted Part IX (Articles 243 - 243O) into the Constitution.

• Panchayats were recognized as institutions of self-government.

• A three-tier Panchayati Raj structure was mandated for rural areas.

• Regular five-year elections to Panchayats were made compulsory.

• State Election Commissions were created to conduct Panchayat elections.

• State Finance Commissions were mandated for fiscal devolution to Panchayats.

• Reservation was provided for SCs, STs, and not less than one-third women.

• The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 relates to Urban Local Bodies, not Panchayats.

• The 74th Amendment inserted Part IXA, covering Municipalities in urban areas.

• The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 is known as the Mini-Constitution and focused on centralization, Fundamental Duties, and Directive Principles.

• The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978 restored civil liberties curtailed during the Emergency.

• The 44th Amendment dealt mainly with Fundamental Rights and Emergency provisions.

• Only the 73rd Amendment specifically institutionalized rural local self-governance in India.

The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 introduces significant digital integration in criminal procedure to improve speed, transparency, and accessibility of justice delivery. The provision for e-FIR, e-summons, and e-warrants reflects a shift toward technology-driven policing and judicial processes.

Key Points:

• BNSS, 2023 replaces the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

• It emphasizes digital and electronic modes of legal processes.

• e-FIR enables online registration of complaints.

• e-summons and e-warrants reduce procedural delays.

• Digital systems enhance citizen accessibility to justice.

• Technology reduces dependence on physical paperwork.

• Electronic records improve traceability and accountability.

• The reforms align with Digital India initiatives.

• Police - court coordination is strengthened through online platforms.

• BNSS reflects modernization of criminal justice administration.

The Green Revolution in India was initiated during the Third Five-Year Plan (1961 - 1966) with the objective of achieving self-sufficiency in foodgrain production. The plan emphasized the adoption of High-Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds, expansion of irrigation, and increased use of fertilizers and modern agricultural practices, particularly for wheat and rice.

Key Points:

• The Third Five-Year Plan covered the period 1961 - 1966.

• Its primary objective was self-reliance and growth, especially in agriculture.

• The Green Revolution was launched to address chronic food shortages.

• Introduction of HYV seeds marked a shift to technology-intensive farming.

• Emphasis was placed on irrigation, fertilizers, and pesticides.

• Wheat and rice were the main crops targeted initially.

• Punjab, Haryana, and western Uttar Pradesh became early Green Revolution regions.

• The Second Five-Year Plan (1956 - 1961) focused on heavy industrialization based on the Mahalanobis model, not agricultural transformation.

• The Second Plan prioritized steel plants, machine tools, and capital goods industries.

• The Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969 - 1974) emphasized growth with stability and self-reliance, consolidating gains made earlier.

• The Fourth Plan focused on redistribution with growth, not the introduction of Green Revolution technology.

• The Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974 - 1979) aimed at poverty removal (Garibi Hatao) and employment generation.

• The Fifth Plan emphasized social objectives rather than agricultural technological change.

• The Green Revolution fundamentally transformed India's agrarian economy during the Third Plan period.

• It reduced dependence on food imports and improved national food security.

A negative power (-2.5 dioptre) indicates the use of a concave (diverging) lens, which is prescribed for myopia. In this condition, distant objects appear blurred because the image forms in front of the retina.

Key Points:

• Myopia is also known as nearsightedness.

• Distant objects appear blurred, while near objects are clear.

• The image forms in front of the retina.

• It is corrected using a concave (diverging) lens.

• Lens power for myopia is negative.

• -2.5 D indicates moderate myopia.

• Myopia may result from elongation of the eyeball.

• It is a common refractive error of the eye.

• Spectacles help refocus light onto the retina.

• Proper correction improves distance vision clarity.

questions.question: Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful passage: 1) Marine ecosystems are sensitive to temperature shifts.2. Coral bleaching is one visible consequence.3. Rising ocean temperatures disrupt symbiotic algae.4. This affects reef biodiversity and fisheries.
questions.questionHtml:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful passage:

1) Marine ecosystems are sensitive to temperature shifts.2. Coral bleaching is one visible consequence.3. Rising ocean temperatures disrupt symbiotic algae.4. This affects reef biodiversity and fisheries.
questions.solution:
The paragraph follows a clear general statement → cause → effect → consequence sequence.

Sentence 1 is the correct opening sentence because it introduces the broad topic - the sensitivity of marine ecosystems - without any reference words.

Sentence 3 logically follows by explaining the cause, i.e., rising ocean temperatures disrupting symbiotic algae.

Sentence 2 then presents a specific visible effect, namely coral bleaching, which directly results from the disruption mentioned earlier.

Sentence 4 acts as the concluding sentence, with "This" referring back to coral bleaching and explaining its wider impact on reef biodiversity and fisheries.

Why the other options are incorrect

1) 3-2-1-4 - starts with a cause before introducing the general context.

3) 2-3-1-4 - begins with an effect without explaining the cause.

4) 1-2-3-4 - places the cause after the effect, disrupting logical flow.

Final coherent order:

1 → 3 → 2 → 4

questions.question: Rearrange the following sentences in correct order to make a logical passage. 1) This allows scientists to study distant galaxies. 2) The Hubble Space Telescope revolutionized astronomy. 3) It provides unprecedented clear images of the universe. 4) Its data has led to numerous groundbreaking discoveries.
questions.questionHtml:
Rearrange the following sentences in correct order to make a logical passage.

1) This allows scientists to study distant galaxies.

2) The Hubble Space Telescope revolutionized astronomy.

3) It provides unprecedented clear images of the universe.

4) Its data has led to numerous groundbreaking discoveries.
questions.solution:
The passage follows a coherent Introduction → Explanation → Result → Conclusion structure.

Sentence 2 is the correct opening sentence because it introduces the main subject, the Hubble Space Telescope, in a general, non-referential manner.

Sentence 3 logically follows by explaining how Hubble revolutionized astronomy - by providing unprecedentedly clear images of the universe.

Sentence 1 then states the direct result of those clear images, i.e., enabling scientists to study distant galaxies.

Sentence 4 serves as the concluding sentence, summarizing the broader impact and significance of Hubble's data through its groundbreaking discoveries.

Why the other options are incorrect

1) 2-1-3-4 - introduces a result before explaining the mechanism (clear images).

2) 2-4-1-3 - jumps to conclusions before explaining how the telescope functions.

3) 3-4-2-1 - begins with explanation without introducing the subject.

Final correct sequence:

2 → 3 → 1 → 4

questions.question: A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech. She said that the seminar had been postponed indefinitely.
questions.questionHtml:
A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech.

She said that the seminar had been postponed indefinitely.

options.text: She said, "The seminar has been postponed indefinitely."
options.html: She said, "The seminar has been postponed indefinitely."

options.text: She said, "The seminar was postponed indefinitely."
options.html: She said, "The seminar was postponed indefinitely."

options.text: She said, "The seminar had been postponed indefinitely."
options.html: She said, "The seminar had been postponed indefinitely."

questions.solution:
Tense=>

Past perfect passive (had been postponed) reported after a past reporting verb (said).

When converting to direct speech, if the original statement is not tied to present relevance, the past perfect can be retained to preserve the exact meaning and time reference.

Why the other options are incorrect

1) Changes had been to has been, altering time reference.

2) Oversimplifies tense and omits "indefinitely."

3) Shifts to simple past, losing the prior-time emphasis.

Correct Direct:

She said, "The seminar had been postponed indefinitely."

questions.question: A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech. She said to me, "Have you completed the assignment?"

A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech.

options.text: She said me had I completed the assignment.
options.html: She said me had I completed the assignment.

questions.solution:

Present perfect → past perfect (tense backshift due to past reporting verb).

Structure

Yes/No question → asked + whether/if + subject + verb (statement order).

Option (3) correctly changes said to → asked, uses whether, applies tense backshift, and maintains proper word order.

Why the other options are incorrect

1) Fails to backshift the tense.

2) Retains present perfect after a past reporting verb.

4) Incorrect verb form and structure.

Correct Indirect:

She asked me whether I had completed the assignment.

questions.question: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: Had the memorandum been clearer, (1)/ the committee might have postponed (2)/ or even cancel (3)/ the meeting for further deliberation. (4)
questions.questionHtml:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

Had the memorandum been clearer, (1)/ the committee might have postponed (2)/ or even cancel (3)/ the meeting for further deliberation. (4)
questions.solution:
The error lies in "or even cancel."

There must be parallel verb structure after the modal phrase "might have". Both verbs should be in the base form following have.

The phrase should be "might have postponed or even cancelled" (or postponed .. cancelled), not a mix of have + past participle and bare verb.

Why the other parts are correct

1) Correct conditional inversion ("Had the memorandum been clearer").

2) Correct modal perfect construction.

4) Grammatically correct infinitive phrase.

Corrected sentence:

Had the memorandum been clearer, the committee might have postponed or even cancelled the meeting for further deliberation.

questions.question: Select the correct option: No sooner had the verdict been announced __ the gallery erupted in applause.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct option:

No sooner had the verdict been announced __ the gallery erupted in applause.
questions.solution:
The correlative structure "No sooner.. than" is a fixed grammatical construction used to show immediate sequence.

Why the other options are incorrect

1) when - incorrect with "no sooner."

3) once - does not fit the correlative structure.

4) but - grammatically incorrect here.

Other important correlative pairs:

• Hardly / Scarcely / Barely .. when → immediate past action

Hardly had he arrived when the meeting began.

• Not only .. but also → emphasis + addition

She is not only intelligent but also hardworking.

• Either .. or → choice

You must either apologize or face consequences.

• Neither .. nor → negative pairing

He neither called nor replied.

• Such .. that → result

It was such a storm that flights were cancelled.

• So .. that → degree + result

The lecture was so boring that students left.

• Whether .. or → alternatives

I don't know whether he will come or not.
